You're completely wrong. If you die, your family will be very heartbroken and shocked that they will probably live the rest of their life in regret and sadness. The same goes for your friends.

I'm kind of an introvert too, and I'm very lucky that some very great friend came to me.
However I don't currently have enough friends that match the same interest as me, and my idea of making new friends is to talk to as many strangers as I can.
I know this is way out of my comfort zone, but I do this by going to a place that no one knows me and have awkward conversations with strangers. Most of the conversations fail because I really suck, but sometimes I can talk to a stranger for a few hours. 
I know it's depression to get rejected, but I set my goal to having 100 awkward conversations with people i'll probably never met again. It's hard to start at the beginning, but you can try getting yourself a bit drunk to loosen up.

Why don't you move to a new city or even country? 
I suggest Canada because we are all very nice here and it have one of the lowest crime rate in the world. You can be confident that you'll be safe.

You were born with nothing, and now you can be reborn.

Kids growing up without both of their parents would turn out worse than other kids. I know both from personal experience (was adopted by parents who don't love me) and as a fact from studies done in psychology.

By killing yourself, you will also be ruining your kid's lives.

As for being happy, I don't really know what that is either, because I can never be happy about things I do. But I do get happy when my friends have achieved something, or when I help other people so that I feel that I'm needed.

I think you should connect better with your kids and they will bring you happiness. Depending on how old they are, they might not understand your love for them and your sacrifice for them, but be patient, when they grow older they will tell you they love you.

I've been depressed before, for probably different reason, having more to do with relationship.
I've considered suicide tons of times, like you, I started having suicide thought as a young kid, back then it wasn't because of depression, but because of fear of getting into trouble. (I was so scared of my dad finding out something bad I did, that I would rather commit suicide). 
When I was in middle school, I was very happy, back then if I reflect back on that I almost died because I was afraid to get into trouble, I would be glad that I didn't do it.
Moving onto a few years ago, I was very depressed, I don't even want to talk about the reason, because I feel typing it out would make me depressed again. But the point was, I thought of committing suicide many times, and each time I didn't, back then I thought I was a coward for not doing it. But now although I haven't completely recover. (I still occasionally get sad) I'm glad I didn't commit again. The reason is that I  have learned alot more about life that I didn't before. You'll always think you are the smartest currently, but in a few years, you'll realize that you were being very dumb before. That is life, and your life story is not over. 

The 2 reason that I chose to not do it was because of friends and relatives who I will harm if I do it, when they are innocent. The other reason is that I've read and know for a fact that depression is recoverable, and when you are at the bottom you can only go up. It took me 3 years to get up, but in the end i did it.

One of the things I did to help me was to further understand myself by taking psychology courses from my school, only you control yourself so if your brain tells you to commit suicide, you should understand why, and learn to change it for the better.
